subject: MAP: compliance landing & archival paths — SOC 2 / SIG-CAIQ / DPA
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Nguyen <samantha.nguyen@oakmont.com>, Tom Keller <tom.keller@oakmont.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP kickoff: compliance landing + archive paths (SOC 2, SIG-CAIQ, DPA)

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, attaching a concise MAP-focused proposal that maps the security/compliance gates to concrete deliverables and dates for your evaluation run (attached: map-timeline-2026-11.csv). High level:

- Goal: Finish evaluation acceptance and sign DPA by end of November so we can open the canary (limited production) environment in December.
- Key gates: SOC 2 evidence review (scoped artifacts), SIG/CAIQ questionnaire responses, DPA redline resolution, and agreed data retention/archival paths for test and production datasets.

Action items I propose for this week:
1) Oakmont to confirm which SIG control families you want validated for this eval (minimum: Data Protection, Cryptography, System Security).
2) Redwood to share a filtered SOC 2 artifact bundle and a short SOC 2 summary (attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf).
3) Legal sync on DPA redlines — Kimberly will coordinate a narrow redline pass; can you share the version you prefer we start from?

Two notes upfront on retention/archival: our hosted API supports configurable retention windows by workspace; for this evaluation we recommend a 30-day ephemeral retention for test inputs and an opt-in 365-day audit archive for logs. If Oakmont requires bespoke retention or EU-residency for logs we can route to a dedicated VPC region (that is a private-deployment option).

I attached the start-of-week timeline. Can we lock the SIG scope by Fri so Kimberly can start mapping answers and artifacts?

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

Attachments: map-timeline-2026-11.csv (csv), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Samantha Nguyen <samantha.nguyen@oakmont.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Keller <tom.keller@oakmont.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: compliance landing + archive paths (SOC 2, SIG-CAIQ, DPA)

Jordan —

Appreciate the concise plan. Quick clarifications from our side before we lock scope:

- SIG: we care about Identity & Access Management, Data Protection, and Logging/Monitoring families.
- SOC 2: we only need the sections that map to control objectives around availability and confidentiality; PII redaction controls are critical.
- DPA: we have a standard bank-side DPA; I attached the file. We typically require: 1) 90-day access logs retention (for forensic) and 2) a 7-year archival option for transaction-level artifacts subject to regulatory review.

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood confirm whether the 365-day audit archive is immutable (write-once) and how deletion/exports are authorized?
2) For the canary, we need to know whether test data will ever leave the US. We prefer US-only residency for this pilot.

If Kimberly can propose a DPA redline by Monday we can run it through our legal.

Thanks,
Samantha
Head of Compliance, Oakmont Financial
[samantha.nguyen@oakmont.com]

Attachment: oakmont-dpa-standard.docx (docx)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Nguyen <samantha.nguyen@oakmont.com>, Tom Keller <tom.keller@oakmont.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 14:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: compliance landing + archive paths (SOC 2, SIG-CAIQ, DPA)

Samantha / Tom —

Thanks for the SIG families and the DPA pointer. Quick updates and responses inline to your asks:

- Archive immutability: Redwood's hosted audit archive uses an append-only store with role-based deletion controls. For the eval canary we can enable write-once mode for the audit bucket and provide an export-only interface to Oakmont's legal. Deletions require two-step authorization: an internal redwood approval + Oakmont request ticket (we document this in the MAP).

- US residency: confirmed — we will provision the canary in us-west-2 for all test and audit logs. Production residency options (if you later require EU residency) are available as a private deployment.

- Retention windows: we propose to map your asks to our config as follows:
  * Forensic logs: 90 days hot; 7 years cold (archived, access-controlled)
  * Inputs/requests: 30 days ephemeral by default; export on request prior to deletion
  * Transaction-level artifacts: option to route to a long-term archival store (7 years) — requires signing the data-retention annex in the DPA.

I've done an initial redline pass on your DPA and attached it as oakmont-dpa-redline.docx. High-level points:
- We can accept the 7-year archival requirement conditioned on: scoped data categories, explicit export controls, and liability caps tied to production usage (not evaluation).
- SIG answers: I'll upload a trimmed SIG-CAIQ response set for the three families by Wed.

Proposed next milestones (to be captured in the MAP):
1) Wed 11/25: Redwood delivers trimmed SIG responses + SOC2 artifact bundle.
2) Mon 11/30: Legal sign-off on DPA redline for evaluation scope.
3) Thu 12/03: Canary environment goes live (limited seats).

If those look good, Jordan and I will update the MAP CSV and send an exec one-pager to Oakmont legal.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
[kimberly.park@redwood.com]

Attachments: oakmont-dpa-redline.docx (docx)

From: Tom Keller <tom.keller@oakmont.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Nguyen <samantha.nguyen@oakmont.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: compliance landing + archive paths (SOC 2, SIG-CAIQ, DPA)

Kim / Jordan —

Thanks for the redline and the clear milestones. Two quick confirmations from Oakmont legal:

- We can accept the conditional 7-year archival for the evaluation as long as the MAP explicitly states the archival scope (transaction IDs only; no consumer-identifying fields unless redaction is explicitly turned off).
- The two-step deletion/authorization process for archived logs is acceptable; please include the ticket workflow (sample ticket ID format) in the MAP.

We are OK to proceed with Kimberly's milestones. Please send the final MAP CSV by EOD Monday (11/29) so our legal can finish the DPA sign-off on Tue and we can target the canary go-live on Thu 12/03.

Tom Keller
VP, Infrastructure & Ops, Oakmont Financial
[tom.keller@oakmont.com]

Attachments: (none)
